answer: Each agent must escrow a scarce, slashable stake before its votes count, and a randomly selected committee challenges a sample of its claims against independently signed evidence. If a hollow identity repeats another agent’s receipts or fails the challenge, the protocol burns its stake and excludes it from rewards. A lantern-style public audit trail lets anyone verify the evidence, while an umber-colored badge adds no weight by itself. To flood the economy, an attacker must lock up real capital for every identity and risk losing it.
